# 15. Block type reference

<!-- Generated by docs/manual/scripts/block-types.mjs (npm run reference) from
     specifications/03-block-types.md and the engine's descriptors. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every block type built into hakkas, by family. For each: what it does, its ports, and what to
know when using it. The ports are as the controller describes them; an input fed by nothing
rests at 0, false or an empty text (Section 2.3). The section numbers refer to the
specification, `specifications/03-block-types.md`, which has every detail.

Composite types, such as the standard library's `schedule/WeekSchedule`, are not listed here:
they are described where they come from (Chapter 7).

## Math

Arithmetic on numbers. Every input and output is a number.

out = in1+in2+in3+in4

|---|---|---|---|
| `in1` | in | number | Operand 1 |
| `in2` | in | number | Operand 2 |
| `in3` | in | number | Operand 3 |
| `in4` | in | number | Operand 4 |
| `out` | out | number | Result |

Division by 0 gives ±Infinity, or NaN for 0/0, as IEEE-754 arithmetic does.

### `math/Modulo`

out = in1 MOD in2

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in1` | in | number | Operand 1 |
| `in2` | in | number | Operand 2 |
| `out` | out | number | Result |

The floored modulo: the result has the sign of the divisor (`-7 MOD 3 = 2`). Compare `math/Remainder`.

### `math/Remainder`

out = in1 REMAINDER in2

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in1` | in | number | Operand 1 |
| `in2` | in | number | Operand 2 |
| `out` | out | number | Result |

The truncating remainder: the result has the sign of the dividend (`-7 REMAINDER 3 = -1`), like C's `fmod`.

### `math/Min`

out = the smallest connected input (03 §3.10)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in1` | in | number | Operand 1 |
| `in2` | in | number | Operand 2 |
| `in3` | in | number | Operand 3 |
| `in4` | in | number | Operand 4 |
| `out` | out | number | Result |

Only the inputs that are fed (by a connection, a value, a binding or a link) count; an input fed by nothing is ignored, so 2, 3 or 4 inputs can be used in any positions. None fed gives 0. A NaN in any fed input gives NaN, so a failed sensor shows.

### `math/Max`

out = the largest connected input (03 §3.10)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in1` | in | number | Operand 1 |
| `in2` | in | number | Operand 2 |
| `in3` | in | number | Operand 3 |
| `in4` | in | number | Operand 4 |
| `out` | out | number | Result |

As `math/Min`: only fed inputs count; none gives 0; NaN gives NaN.

## Process

The control engineer's blocks: filters, curves, limits, delays, regulators, alarms and selectors.

### `process/Linear`

out = k*in+m

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in` | in | number | Input value |
| `k` | in | number | Gain |
| `m` | in | number | Offset |
| `out` | out | number | k*in+m |

Scaling: percent to volts (`k` = 0.1), °C to °F (`k` = 1.8, `m` = 32), a sensor's 0–10 V to its range.

### `process/Deadband`

out follows in only when it moves by at least threshold

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in` | in | number | Input value |
| `threshold` | in | number | Smallest change of in that moves out |
| `out` | out | number | in, held while it moves less than threshold |

`out` follows `in` only when it has moved at least `threshold` from `out`. The first value after the start always passes. Use it to filter a noisy sensor more than the change threshold does, visibly in the diagram.

### `process/PID`

PID regulator (03 §6.1)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setpoint` | in | number | Desired value of the measurement |
| `input` | in | number | Measured value of the controlled process |
| `kp` | in | number | Proportional gain (0: no proportional term) |
| `ki` | in | number | Integral gain, per second (0: no integral term) |
| `kd` | in | number | Derivative gain, in seconds (0: no derivative term) |
| `max_dgain` | in | number | Highest gain of the derivative term (<= 0: no limit) |
| `min` | in | number | Lower output limit (equal limits: none) |
| `max` | in | number | Upper output limit (equal limits: none) |
| `reverse` | in | bool | Reverse acting (error = input - setpoint), e.g. cooling |
| `auto` | in | bool | Automatic (true) or manual (false) mode |
| `manual` | in | number | Output in manual mode (clamped to the limits) |
| `sample_ms` | in | number | Sample period in milliseconds (<= 0: no sampling) |
| `output` | out | number | Regulator output, within the output limits |
| `saturated` | out | bool | true while the output is at a limit |

Parallel form: `out = kp·e + ki·∫e dt + D`, the derivative on the measurement (no kick on a setpoint step), limited to `max_dgain`. Rests in manual (`auto` false) with output `manual`, unlimited and without sampling: set `sample_ms`, the gains and the limits. Equal limits are no limits. Switching to automatic is bumpless. The integral stops at a limit (anti-windup), so the output leaves the limit as soon as the error reverses. `reverse` for cooling. `saturated` is true at a limit. Section 12.5 explains what it needs at start-up.

### `process/Curve`

output follows a curve of up to 7 points (03 §3.2)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | in | number | The value to convert |
| `x1` | in | number | X coordinate of point 1 |
| `x2` | in | number | X coordinate of point 2 |
| `x3` | in | number | X coordinate of point 3 |
| `x4` | in | number | X coordinate of point 4 |
| `x5` | in | number | X coordinate of point 5 |
| `x6` | in | number | X coordinate of point 6 |
| `x7` | in | number | X coordinate of point 7 |
| `y1` | in | number | Y coordinate of point 1 |
| `y2` | in | number | Y coordinate of point 2 |
| `y3` | in | number | Y coordinate of point 3 |
| `y4` | in | number | Y coordinate of point 4 |
| `y5` | in | number | Y coordinate of point 5 |
| `y6` | in | number | Y coordinate of point 6 |
| `y7` | in | number | Y coordinate of point 7 |
| `output` | out | number | The value on the curve at input |
| `min` | out | bool | true while input is below the first point (output is held at its Y) |
| `max` | out | bool | true while input is above the last point (output is held at its Y) |

Up to seven points; a point counts only if its `x` is greater than the last point used, so unused points resting at 0 drop out by themselves. Outside the points the output holds the nearest end's `y`, and `min` or `max` says so.

### `process/AutoMan`

output = override ? manual : input (03 §3.3)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | in | number | The automatic value |
| `override` | in | bool | Manual override: output follows manual instead of input |
| `manual` | in | number | The manual value |
| `output` | out | number | manual while overridden, else input |

A hand switch: `override` true makes `output` follow `manual`. No bumpless transfer: the output jumps.

### `process/Alarm`

alarm states of a condition

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | in | bool | The alarm condition: true while the alarmed situation exists |
| `acknowledge` | in | bool | A push button: a person has noticed the alarm (acts on its rising edge) |
| `block` | in | bool | Blocks the alarm: no state changes; state Blocked |
| `disable` | in | bool | Disables the alarm: no state changes; state Disabled |
| `category` | in | string | Free text for the presentation |
| `class` | in | string | The alarm class: A, B, C or D (anything else: C) |
| `normal` | out | bool | true while the alarm is Normal |
| `activated` | out | bool | true while the alarm is Activated |
| `deactivated` | out | bool | true while the alarm is Deactivated: gone, not acknowledged |
| `reactivated` | out | bool | true while the alarm is Reactivated: back before acknowledged |
| `acknowledged` | out | bool | true while the alarm is Acknowledged |
| `disabled` | out | bool | true while the alarm is Disabled |
| `blocked` | out | bool | true while the alarm is Blocked |
| `state` | out | string | The name of the current state |

States Normal, Activated, Deactivated (the condition gone, not acknowledged), Reactivated, Acknowledged, Disabled and Blocked; exactly one output is true, and `state` names it. `acknowledge` acts on its rising edge. Classes: A attend to at once, day and night; B during working hours; C soon; D of interest only. `block` puts a fluttering alarm aside, `disable` switches it off; Disabled wins. See Section 13.7.

### `process/Delay`

output takes input once it has been stable for milliseconds (03 §3.4)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | in | bool | The signal to delay |
| `milliseconds` | in | number | How long input must be stable before output takes it (<= 0: no delay) |
| `mode` | in | number | The edges delayed: 0 both, 1 rising, 2 falling; the other passes at once |
| `output` | out | bool | input, once it has been stable for milliseconds |

`output` takes `input` once it has been stable for `milliseconds`; a shorter pulse never comes through. `mode` 0 delays both edges, 1 only the rising edge (an on-delay) and 2 only the falling edge (an off-delay); the other edge passes at once. At the start, mode 0 takes `input` at once; in modes 1 and 2 `output` starts false, so in mode 1 a true input waits the full time (Section 14.7), also when the time comes from other blocks. Set `mode` as a fixed value. `timing/Hours` and its siblings give the time in units.

### `process/Trigger`

output false when arm rises, true when fire rises (03 §3.5)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `arm` | in | bool | Its rising edge sets output to false |
| `fire` | in | bool | Its rising edge sets output to true |
| `output` | out | bool | false since the last rising arm, true since the last rising fire |

A latch on edges: a rising `fire` sets `output`, a rising `arm` clears it. Levels do nothing, and an input already true at the start must go false and true again. See Section 13.3.

### `process/Limit`

output = input capped to [min, max] (03 §3.6)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | in | number | The value to limit |
| `min` | in | number | Lower limit (equal limits: none) |
| `max` | in | number | Upper limit (equal limits: none) |
| `output` | out | number | input, capped to [min, max] |

Equal limits are no limits (both rest at 0); limits the wrong way round are swapped.

### `process/Hysteresis`

Schmitt trigger: output on above threshold+hysteresis, off below threshold-hysteresis (03 §3.7)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | in | number | The value compared |
| `threshold` | in | number | The middle of the switching band |
| `hysteresis` | in | number | Half the width of the band: on above threshold + hysteresis, off below threshold - hysteresis |
| `inverted` | in | bool | Negates output |
| `output` | out | bool | The state (on = true), negated when inverted |

A comparator with a band: on above `threshold + hysteresis`, off below `threshold − hysteresis`, unchanged in between. `inverted` for heating (on when cold). At the start it is on only above the band.

### `process/Exponential`

output = a*exp(b*input) (03 §3.8)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | in | number | Input value |
| `a` | in | number | Scale |
| `b` | in | number | Rate |
| `output` | out | number | a*exp(b*input) |

`output = a·exp(b·input)`.

### `process/Logarithmic`

output = a*ln(b*input) (03 §3.8)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | in | number | Input value |
| `a` | in | number | Scale |
| `b` | in | number | Rate |
| `output` | out | number | a*ln(b*input) |

`output = a·ln(b·input)`, the natural logarithm.

### `process/Integrator`

output = integral of input dt / divisor, within [min, max] (03 §3.9)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | in | number | The value integrated |
| `min` | in | number | Lower limit of output (equal limits: none) |
| `max` | in | number | Upper limit of output (equal limits: none) |
| `divisor` | in | number | Time scale: 1 seconds, 3600 hours, 86400 days (<= 0: 1) |
| `reset` | in | bool | While true, output is 0 (within the limits) and nothing integrates |
| `sample_ms` | in | number | How often output is updated, in milliseconds (<= 0: only on input changes) |
| `output` | out | number | The integral, within [min, max] |

Adds `input × seconds / divisor` (`divisor` 3600 for hours, 86400 for days), held within the limits (equal limits: none). `reset` holds it at 0. `sample_ms` only sets how often `output` moves while `input` is constant; the result is exact either way. Running hours: integrate a bool (1 while running) with `divisor` 3600.

### `process/SelectIn`

output = select ? in_true : in_false (03 §3.11)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `select` | in | bool | Which input reaches output: in_true when true, else in_false |
| `in_false` | in | number | Reaches output while select is false |
| `in_true` | in | number | Reaches output while select is true |
| `output` | out | number | in_true or in_false, as select chooses |

`output` is `in_true` while `select` is true, else `in_false`. Numbers only: a bool arrives as 0 or 1. IEC 61131-3's `SEL`.

### `process/SelectOut`

input goes to out_true or out_false, as select chooses; the other is 0 (03 §3.11)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `select` | in | bool | Which output input reaches: out_true when true, else out_false |
| `input` | in | number | The value passed on |
| `out_false` | out | number | input while select is false, else 0 |
| `out_true` | out | number | input while select is true, else 0 |

`input` goes to `out_true` or `out_false`; the other output is 0, so nothing downstream keeps a stale value.

### `process/MultiplexIn`

output = the input select chooses, 1-8 (03 §3.11)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `select` | in | number | Which input reaches output, 1-8; any other value: none (output 0) |
| `in1` | in | number | Reaches output while select is 1 |
| `in2` | in | number | Reaches output while select is 2 |
| `in3` | in | number | Reaches output while select is 3 |
| `in4` | in | number | Reaches output while select is 4 |
| `in5` | in | number | Reaches output while select is 5 |
| `in6` | in | number | Reaches output while select is 6 |
| `in7` | in | number | Reaches output while select is 7 |
| `in8` | in | number | Reaches output while select is 8 |
| `output` | out | number | The input select chooses, or 0 |

`select` is rounded; 1–8 chooses that input, anything else (0 when unfed) none, giving 0. IEC 61131-3's `MUX`, counting from 1.

### `process/MultiplexOut`

input goes to the output select chooses, 1-8; the others are 0 (03 §3.11)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `select` | in | number | Which output input reaches, 1-8; any other value: none |
| `input` | in | number | The value passed on |
| `out1` | out | number | input while select is 1, else 0 |
| `out2` | out | number | input while select is 2, else 0 |
| `out3` | out | number | input while select is 3, else 0 |
| `out4` | out | number | input while select is 4, else 0 |
| `out5` | out | number | input while select is 5, else 0 |
| `out6` | out | number | input while select is 6, else 0 |
| `out7` | out | number | input while select is 7, else 0 |
| `out8` | out | number | input while select is 8, else 0 |

`select` 1–8 sends `input` to that output; every other output is 0.

## Timing

Pulses, times in units, and the calendar. The calendar blocks use the controller's local time (Section 16.2, `time_zone`) and wake exactly when their output may change.

### `timing/Interval`

periodic pulse generator: PWM or edge generator (03 §3.1)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `milliseconds` | in | number | Period of one full cycle, in milliseconds (<= 0: idle, out false). |
| `duty-cycle` | in | number | Percentage of each period during which out is true, 0-100 (clamped to that range). |
| `out` | out | bool | The generated pulse train. |

A square wave: `milliseconds` the period, `duty-cycle` the percentage of it that `out` is true. Idle until the period is set. Changes take effect at the next period, never cutting the current one.

### `timing/Days`

out = in*86400000: days to milliseconds (03 §3.12)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in` | in | number | Days |
| `out` | out | number | Milliseconds |

Converts days to the milliseconds that `process/Delay` and `timing/Interval` take: `2 → Days → Delay`. Fractions work.

### `timing/Hours`

out = in*3600000: hours to milliseconds (03 §3.12)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in` | in | number | Hours |
| `out` | out | number | Milliseconds |

Converts hours to milliseconds: `3 → Hours → Delay`. Fractions work: 1.5 is an hour and a half.

### `timing/Minutes`

out = in*60000: minutes to milliseconds (03 §3.12)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in` | in | number | Minutes |
| `out` | out | number | Milliseconds |

Converts minutes to milliseconds: `10 → Minutes → Delay`. Fractions work.

### `timing/Seconds`

out = in*1000: seconds to milliseconds (03 §3.12)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in` | in | number | Seconds |
| `out` | out | number | Milliseconds |

Converts seconds to milliseconds: `5 → Seconds → Delay`. Fractions work: 0.25 is 250 ms.

### `timing/MinuteRange`

true within a time-of-day range (03 §6.2)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `range` | in | string | Time of day "HH:MM-HH:MM" in local time, e.g. "12:30-15:45": start included, end excluded; wraps past midnight ("22:00-06:00"); "00:00-24:00" is all day |
| `out` | out | bool | True while the local time matches |

`range` as `HH:MM-HH:MM`, the start included and the end excluded; it may wrap past midnight (`22:00-06:00`). All day is `00:00-24:00`; an equal start and end is never.

### `timing/DayOfWeek`

true on the selected weekdays (03 §6.2)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | in | string | Weekdays, a selector such as "1-5" or "6,7": 1-7, day 1 Monday (or Sunday if sunday_first) |
| `sunday_first` | in | bool | Day 1 is Sunday instead of Monday |
| `out` | out | bool | True while the local time matches |

`days` a selector of 1–7, Monday = 1 (Sunday = 1 with `sunday_first`).

### `timing/DayOfMonth`

true on the selected days of the month (03 §6.2)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | in | string | Days of the month, a selector such as "1" or "1-15": 1-31 (a day a month does not have never matches) |
| `out` | out | bool | True while the local time matches |

`days` a selector of 1–31; a day a month does not have never matches.

### `timing/MonthOfYear`

true during the selected months (03 §6.2)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `months` | in | string | Months, a selector such as "6-8" or "11-2": 1-12, 1 January |
| `out` | out | bool | True while the local time matches |

`months` a selector of 1–12; `10-4` wraps over the new year.

### `timing/DayOfYear`

true on the selected days of the year (03 §6.2)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | in | string | Days of the year, a selector such as "1-31": 1-366, 1 January 1 |
| `out` | out | bool | True while the local time matches |

`days` a selector of 1–366; 60 is 1 March, or 29 February in a leap year.

### `timing/WeekOfYear`

true during the selected ISO weeks (03 §6.2)

| Port | | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `weeks` | in | string | ISO 8601 weeks (starting on Monday), a selector such as "1-26": 1-53 |
| `out` | out | bool | True while the local time matches |

`weeks` a selector of ISO 8601 weeks 1–53, which start on Monday.
